content.title: Aluminum Fee Is Likely to Stay High, Even With Tariff Relief
content.summary: Alcoa says the tariff-inflated premiums that U.S. aluminum buyers are paying likely won’t recede even if a deal is reached this year to scale back the 50% duty on aluminum from Canada.  Canada is the largest supplier of imported aluminum to the U.S., but it isn't the only one.  As long as the 50% duty remains on imports from other countries, Alcoa Chief Executive William Oplinger said the premium would remain elevated, as suppliers seek to recoup the cost of tariffs.
